body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃgha ahamevaṃnāmā saṃghā tpravrajyopasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ yāce yadupasaṃpādayatu māṃ bhadantaḥ saṃgho 'nukampako 'nukampāmupādāya / [evaṃ trirapi vaktavyam / yācite paścādekena bhikṣuṇā evaṃ karaṇīyaṃ niṣadya prajñāpitavyam /] śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ saṃghātpravrajyopasaṃpadadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ yācate /
body.translated_text: May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. I, named so-and-so, request from the <s>Saṅgha</s> <s>pravrajyā</s> (going-forth) and <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination) to become a <s>bhikṣu</s>. May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> ordain me, the compassionate one, out of compassion. [This should be said three times. After the petition, one <s>bhikṣu</s> should do as follows: sitting, he should announce:] May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. So-and-so requests from the <s>Saṅgha</s> <s>pravrajyā</s> and <s>upasaṃpad</s> to become a <s>bhikṣu</s>.

body.text: sacetsaṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣamate anujānīyātsaṃgho yatsaṃgha evaṃnāmānaṃ pravrājayate upasaṃpādayedeṣā jñaptiḥ / [evaṃ hi kāryam /] śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ayamevaṃnāmā saṃghāt pravrajyopasaṃpadaṃ [bhikṣubhāvaṃ] yācate tatsaṃghaḥ evaṃnāmānaṃ pravrājayati upasaṃpādayati / yeṣāmāyuṣmatāṃ kṣamate evaṃnāmānaṃ pravrājayantaṃ upasaṃpādayituṃ te tūṣṇīm / yeṣāṃ na kṣamate te bhāṣantām / [iyaṃ prathamā karmavācanā / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi /] pravrājitaṃ upasaṃpāditamevaṃnāmā saṃghena kṣāntamanujñātaṃ yasmāttūṣṇīmevametaddhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: If it is the proper time and the <s>Saṅgha</s> approves, let the <s>Saṅgha</s> consent to ordain and fully ordain so-and-so. This is the <s>jñapti</s> (motion). [Thus should it be done.] May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. This so-and-so requests from the <s>Saṅgha</s> <s>pravrajyā</s> and <s>upasaṃpad</s> [to become a <s>bhikṣu</s>]. The <s>Saṅgha</s> ordains so-and-so and grants full ordination. Those venerable ones who approve of ordaining and fully ordaining so-and-so should remain silent. Those who do not approve should speak. [This is the first <s>karmavācanā</s> (formal proclamation). Likewise a second and third time.] So-and-so has been ordained and fully ordained by the <s>Saṅgha</s>; it is approved and consented to, since they are silent. Thus I record it.

body.text: [eṣa hi pūrvavidhiḥ /] samanvāhara ahamevaṃnāmā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam / dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam / saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam / upāsakaṃ māṃ bhadanto dhārayatu yāvajjīvam / samanvāhara ācārya yathā te āryāḥ arhanto yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātātprativiratā evamahamevaṃnāmā yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇānipātātprativiramāmi / anenāhaṃ prathamenāṅgena teṣāmāryāṇāmarhatāṃ śikṣāyāmanuśikṣe anuvidhīye anukaromi / yathā te āryāḥ yāvajjīvamadattādānaṃ kāmamithyācāraṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānaṃ prahāya surāmaireyapramādasthānātprativiratāḥ evamevāhamevaṃnāmā yāvajjīvamadattādānaṃ kāmamithyācāraṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānaṃ prahāya surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānātprativiramāmi / anena pañcamenāṅgena teṣāmāryāṇāmarhatāṃ śikṣāyāmanuśikṣe anuvidhīye anukaromi / bhadantāḥ samanvāhriyaṃtāṃ ayamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmraḥ [upādhyāyāt] gṛhītāvadātavasanaḥ anavatāritakeśaśmaśrurākāṃkṣate svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitum / soyamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena svākhyāte dharmavinaye keśaśmaśruvatārya kāṣāyāṇi vasrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanāgārikāṃ pravrajisyati / kiṃ pravrajatu / samanvāhara ācārya ahamevaṃnāmā ācāryamupādhyāyaṃ yāce /
body.translated_text: [This is the preliminary procedure.] Attend well: I, so-and-so, go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds. I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among that which is free from passion. I go for refuge to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the foremost among assemblies. May the venerable one consider me an <s>upāsaka</s> (lay follower) for as long as I live. Attend well, teacher: just as those noble <s>Arhats</s> have abandoned the taking of life for as long as they live and abstain from <s>prāṇātipāta</s> (killing living beings), so I, so-and-so, for as long as I live, abstain from the taking of life. By this first precept I train in, follow, and emulate the training of those noble <s>Arhats</s>. Just as those noble ones have for life abandoned <s>adattādāna</s> (taking what is not given), <s>kāma-mithyācāra</s> (sexual misconduct), <s>mṛṣāvāda</s> (false speech), and <s>surā-maireya-madya-pramāda-sthāna</s> (the basis of heedlessness through liquor, spirits, and intoxicants), and abstain from the basis of heedlessness through liquor, spirits, and intoxicants—so I, so-and-so, for as long as I live, abandon the taking of what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and the basis of heedlessness through liquor, spirits, and intoxicants, and abstain from the basis of heedlessness through liquor, spirits, and intoxicants. By this fifth precept I train in, follow, and emulate the training of those noble <s>Arhats</s>. Venerable ones, attend well: this so-and-so, with such-and-such a name, [from the <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor)], wearing white garments, with hair and beard unshaven, wishes to go forth in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. This so-and-so, with such-and-such as his <s>upādhyāya</s>, having shaved his hair and beard in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> and donned the saffron robes, with right faith, will go forth from the household life to the houseless life. May he go forth? Attend well, teacher: I, so-and-so, request the teacher as <s>upādhyāya</s>.

body.text: ācāryo me upadhyāyo bhavatu / ācāryeṇa upādhyāyena pravrajiṣyāmi / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā [adyāgre yāvajjīvaṃ] buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam / dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam / saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam / taṃ bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ śākyasiṃhaṃ śākyādhirājaṃ tathāgataṃ arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajāmi / gṛhaliṅgaṃ samutsṛjāmi / pravrajyāliṅgaṃ samādade / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi / samanvāhara bhadanta ahamevaṃnāmā [adyāgre yāvajjīvam] buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam / dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgānāmagryam / saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam / śrāmaṇeraṃ māṃ bhadanto dhārayatu [yāvajjīvam / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi /] samanvāhara ācārya yathā te āryā arhanto yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātātprativiratā evamevāhaṃ evaṃnāmā yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātātprativiramāmi / anenāhaṃ prathamenāṅgena teṣāmāryāṇāmarhatāṃ śikṣāyāmanuśikṣe anuvidhīye anukaromi / yathā te āryāḥ arhanto yāvajjīvamadattādānaṃ abrahmacaryaṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānaṃ nṛtyagītavāditramālāgandhavilepanavarṇakadhāraṇaṃ uccaśayanamahāśayanaṃ jātarūparajatapratigrahaṃ prahāya jātarūparajatapratigrahātprativirataḥ evamevāhaṃ evaṃnāmā yāvajjīvamadattādānamabrahmacaryyaṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānaṃ nṛtyagītavāditramālāgandhavilepanavarṇakadhāraṇaṃ uccaśayanamahāśayanamakālabhojanaṃ jātarūparajatapratigrahaṃ prahāya jātarūparajatapratigrahātprativiramāmi / anenāhaṃ daśamenāṅgena teṣāmāryāṇāmarhatāṃ śikṣāyāmanuśikṣe anuvidhīye anukaromi /
body.translated_text: May the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) be my <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor). With the <s>ācārya</s> as <s>upādhyāya</s> I shall go forth (<s>pravrajiṣyāmi</s>). Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, [from today onward, for as long as I live,] go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds. I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among things free from passion. I go for refuge to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among communities. Following that Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the sovereign of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), who went forth — I go forth after him. I renounce the marks of a householder. I take up the marks of one who has gone forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>). Likewise a second and a third time. Attend to me, Venerable One (<s>bhadanta</s>): I, so-and-so named, [from today onward, for as long as I live,] go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds. I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among things free from passion. I go for refuge to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among communities. May the Venerable One hold me as a novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>) [for as long as I live. Likewise a second and a third time.] Attend to me, <s>ācārya</s>: just as those noble <s>Arhats</s>, having abandoned the taking of life for as long as they live, abstain from the taking of life — even so I, so-and-so named, having abandoned the taking of life for as long as I live, abstain from the taking of life. By this first precept I train in the training of those noble <s>Arhats</s>, I follow their practice, I imitate them. Just as those noble <s>Arhats</s>, having abandoned for as long as they live: taking what is not given, unchastity, false speech, the use of intoxicants — liquor, spirits, and fermented drinks which cause heedlessness, dancing, singing, music, and the wearing of garlands, perfumes, cosmetics, and ornaments, the use of high and luxurious beds, and the acceptance of gold and silver — even so I, so-and-so named, having abandoned for as long as I live: taking what is not given, unchastity, false speech, the use of intoxicants — liquor, spirits, and fermented drinks which cause heedlessness, dancing, singing, music, and the wearing of garlands, perfumes, cosmetics, and ornaments, the use of high and luxurious beds, eating at improper times, and the acceptance of gold and silver — I abstain from the acceptance of gold and silver. By this tenth precept I train in the training of those noble <s>Arhats</s>, I follow their practice, I imitate them.

body.text: samanvāhara bhadanta ahamevaṃnāmā bhadantaṃ upādhyāyaṃ yāce / bhadanto me upādhyāyo bhavatu / bhadantena upādhyāyena upasaṃpatsye / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ cīvaraṃ saṃghāṭīṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi kṛtaniścitaṃ cīvaraṃ paribhogikam / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ cīvaraṃ uttarāsaṃgaṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi kṛtaniścitaṃ cīvaraṃ pāribhogikam / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ cīvaraṃ antarvāsaṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi kṛtaniścitaṃ cīvaraṃ pāribhogikam / samanvāhara upādhyāya idaṃ cīvaraṃ saṃghāṭīṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi / ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥnavaṃ kariṣyāmi / ardhatṛtīyamaṇḍalakaṃ anantarāyeṇa dhāviṣye vitariṣyāmi chetsye saṃbhaṃtsyāmi saṃgranthiṣye seviṣyāmi raṃkṣye / āsevakān vā atra āropayiṣyāmi cīvaraṃ pāribhogikam / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ cīvaraṃ uttarāsaṃgaṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi / ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ saptakaṃ kariṣyāmi / ardhatṛtīyamaṇḍalakaṃ anantarāyeṇa dhāviṣye vitariṣyāmi chetsye saṃbhaṃtsyāmi saṃgranthiṣye seviṣyāmi / raṃkṣye / āsevakān atra āropayiṣyāmi cīvaraṃ pāribhogikam / samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ cīvaraṃ antarvāsaṃ adhitiṣṭhāmi / ākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ pañcakaṃ kariṣyāmi / ardhatṛtīyamaṇḍalakaṃ anantarāyeṇa dhāviṣye vitariṣyāmi chetsye saṃbhaṃtsyāmi saṃgranthiṣye seviṣyāmi raṃkṣye / āsevakānvā atra āropayiṣyāmi cīvaraṃ pāribhogikam /
body.translated_text: Attend to me, Venerable One: I, so-and-so named, request the Venerable One as <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor). May the Venerable One be my <s>upādhyāya</s>. With the Venerable One as <s>upādhyāya</s> I shall receive full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>). Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, designate this robe as my <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe) — a determined robe for personal use. Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, designate this robe as my <s>uttarāsaṅga</s> (upper robe) — a determined robe for personal use. Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, designate this robe as my <s>antarvāsa</s> (inner robe) — a determined robe for personal use. Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I designate this robe as my <s>saṃghāṭī</s>. If I wish, I shall make it ninefold. Without interruption I shall wash, spread out, cut, stitch, sew together, dye, and color the two-and-a-half circles (<s>ardhatṛtīyamaṇḍalaka</s>). Or I shall attach patches (<s>āsevaka</s>) to it — a robe for personal use. Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, designate this robe as my <s>uttarāsaṅga</s>. If I wish, I shall make it sevenfold. Without interruption I shall wash, spread out, cut, stitch, sew together, dye, and color the two-and-a-half circles. I shall attach patches to it — a robe for personal use. Attend to me, <s>upādhyāya</s>: I, so-and-so named, designate this robe as my <s>antarvāsa</s>. If I wish, I shall make it fivefold. Without interruption I shall wash, spread out, cut, stitch, sew together, dye, and color the two-and-a-half circles. Or I shall attach patches to it — a robe for personal use.

body.text: samanvāhara upādhyāya ahamevaṃnāmā idaṃ pātraṃ ṛṣibhājanaṃ bhikṣābhājanaṃ pāribhogikam / evaṃnāmnaivaṃnāmno rahonuśāsakodhīṣṭaḥ ahamevaṃnāmā utsahase tvamevaṃnāmā naivaṃnāmānaṃ rahasi anuśāsituṃ evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena utsahe / śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ayamevaṃnāmā bhikṣurutsahate evaṃnāmānaṃ rahasyanuśāsituṃ evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena / sacetsaṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyāt saṃghaḥ idamevaṃnāmā bhikṣurevaṃnāmānaṃ rahasyanuśāsiṣyati evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena / eṣā jñaptiḥ / śṛṇutvamāyuṣman ayaṃ te bhūtakālaḥ / ayaṃ satyakālaḥ / yaccāhaṃ kiñcitpṛcchāmi tattvayā lajjitena [mā] bhūtvā bhūtaṃ ca bhūtato vaktavyaṃ abhūtaṃ ca abhūtato 'nirveṭhayitavyam / puruṣo 'si /
body.translated_text: Attend, <s>Upādhyāya</s> (preceptor)! I, named so-and-so, [declare that] this is a <s>pātra</s> (bowl), a vessel of the sages, a vessel for alms, for personal use. The one named so-and-so has been chosen by the one named so-and-so as the private instructor. I, named so-and-so — are you, named so-and-so, able to instruct the one named so-and-so in private, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so? I am able. Let the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> (community) hear! This <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) named so-and-so is willing to instruct the one named so-and-so in private, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the <s>Saṃgha</s> and if it approves, let the <s>Saṃgha</s> authorize this: the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so will instruct the one named so-and-so in private, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so. This is the motion. Listen, venerable one! This is the time for truth for you. This is the time for what is real. Whatever I ask you, you must not be ashamed — what is true must be stated as true, and what is untrue must be clarified as untrue. Are you a man?

body.text: puruṣaḥ puruṣendriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ / paripūrṇaviṃśativarṣaḥ / paripūrṇaṃ te tricīvaraṃ pātraṃ ca / jīvataste mātāpitarau / anujñātosi mātāpitṛbhyām / māsi dāsaḥ / mā āhatakaḥ / mā prāptakaḥ / mā vaktavyakaḥ / mā vikrītakaḥ / mā rājabhaṭaḥ / mā rājakilviṣī / mā rājatatthyakārī / mā te rājā pathyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ vā kāritaṃ vā / māsicauro dhajabandhakaḥ / mā śaṇaṭhakaḥ / mā paṇḍakaḥ / mā bhikṣuṇīdūṣakaḥ / mā stenasaṃvāsikaḥ / mā nānāsaṃvāsikaḥ / mā mātṛghātakaḥ / mā pitṛghātakaḥ / mā arhad ghātakaḥ / mā saṃghabhedakaḥ / mā tathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādakaḥ / mā nāgaḥ / [mā paśuḥ /] mā te kasyacitkiñciddeyamalpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā śaknoṣi vā upasampadaṃ dātum / māsi pūrvaṃ pravrajitaḥ / caturṇāṃ pārājikānāmanyatamo 'nyatamāmāpattimāpannaḥ / kaścidasi etarhi pravrajitaḥ samyak te brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ / kiṃnāmā tvam / kiṃnāmā te upādhyāyaḥ / śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman / bhavanti khalu puruṣāṇāmime evaṃrūpāḥ kāye kāyikāḥ ābādhāḥ / tadyathā kuṣṭhaṃ / gaṃḍaḥ / kiṭibhaḥ / kilāsaṃ / dadruḥ kaṃḍuḥ / kacchū / rajatam / viṣūcikā / vicarcikā / hikkā / jvaraḥ / kṣayaḥ / kāsaḥ / śvāsaḥ śoṣaḥ / apasmāro / lohaliṅgam / āṭakkaraḥ / pāṇḍurogaḥ / aṅgavedaḥ / gulmaṃ rudhiraṃ / bhagandaraḥ / arśāṃsi / cchardiḥ / mūtrarogaḥ ślīpadaṃ / klamaḥ / aṅgadāhaḥ / pārśvadāhaḥ / asthibhedaḥ / ekāhikaḥ / dvaitīyakaḥ / traitīyakaḥ / cāturthikaḥ / nityajvaraḥ / viṣamajvaraḥ / sannipātaḥ / mā te evaṃrūpāḥ kāye kāyikā ābādhāḥ saṃvidyante / anye vā evaṃrūpāḥ / yadasi etarhi mayā pṛṣṭaḥ / etadeva sabrahmacāriṇaḥ [vijñāḥ] saṃghamadhye prakṣyanti / tatrāpi tvayā lajjitena [mā] bhūtvā bhūtaṃ bhūtato vaktavyam / abhūtaṃ ca abhūtato nirveṭhayitavyam / tiṣṭha / mā aśabditaḥ āgamiṣyasi / śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ samanuśiṣṭo mayā evaṃnāmā rahasi āntarāyikān dharmān evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena / kimāgacchatu / śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ahamevaṃnāmā arthaheto nāma gṛhṇāmi evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena upasaṃpatprekṣaḥ sīhamevaṃnāmā saṃghādupasaṃpadaṃ yāce evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena / upasaṃpādayatu māṃ bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / anukartuṃ māṃ bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ anukampako 'nukampāmupādāya /
body.translated_text: Are you a man endowed with male faculties? Have you completed twenty years of age? Is your set of three robes and bowl complete? Are your mother and father alive? Have you been given permission by your mother and father? You are not a slave? Not a bondsman? Not a seized person? Not one under sentence? Not a sold person? Not a king's soldier? Not a king's criminal? Not one performing the king's forced labor? Has the king had any punitive action done or caused to be done to you? You are not a thief or a brigand? Not a cheat? Not a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (sexually non-conforming person)? Not one who has corrupted a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun)? Not one who cohabits with a thief? Not one belonging to a different community? Not a matricide? Not a patricide? Not a killer of an <s>Arhat</s> (saint)? Not a splitter of the <s>Saṃgha</s>? Not one who, with malicious intent, has shed the blood of a <s>Tathāgata</s>? Not a <s>nāga</s> (serpent-being)? Not an animal? Have you anything, whether small or great, owed to anyone? Are you able to give the <s>upasampadā</s> (full ordination)? Have you been previously ordained? Have you committed any one of the four <s>pārājika</s> (offenses entailing expulsion) offenses? Are you now going forth? Has your <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate conduct) been properly practiced? What is your name? What is your <s>Upādhyāya's</s> name? Listen, venerable one! There are indeed these kinds of bodily diseases that arise in the bodies of men, namely: leprosy, boils, eczema, white leprosy, ringworm, itch, scabies, consumption, cholera, skin eruption, hiccups, fever, wasting disease, cough, asthma, emaciation, epilepsy, blood disease, skin disease, jaundice, body pain, abdominal tumor, hemorrhage, fistula, piles, vomiting, urinary disease, elephantiasis, exhaustion, burning of the limbs, burning of the sides, bone-splitting pain, quotidian fever, tertian fever, quartan fever, continuous fever, irregular fever, and fever from the conjunction of humors. Do you have any such bodily diseases in your body, or any others of such a kind? Now that you have been questioned by me, the knowledgeable fellow practitioners in the <s>Saṃgha</s> will ask you these same things in the midst of the assembly. There too, you must not be ashamed — what is true must be stated as true, and what is untrue must be clarified as untrue. Stand here. You will come when called. Let the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> hear! The one named so-and-so has been instructed by me in private regarding the obstructive conditions, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so. May he come forward. Let the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> hear! I, named so-and-so, for the sake of this purpose take the name, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so; the one named so-and-so, seeking <s>upasampadā</s> (full ordination), requests from the <s>Saṃgha</s> the <s>upasampadā</s>, by the authority of the <s>Upādhyāya</s> named so-and-so. May the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> ordain me! May the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> show compassion to me, out of compassion!

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ayamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmnaḥ upasaṃpatprekṣaḥ so 'yamevaṃnāmā saṃghādupasaṃpadaṃ yācate evaṃ nāmnopādhyāyena / sacetsaṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyāt saṃghaḥ yadvayaṃ evaṃnāmānaṃ saṃghamadhye āntarāyikān dharmān pṛcchema evanāmnopādhyāyena / eṣā jñaptiḥ / śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman ayaṃ te pūrvavat sarvam / śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ayamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmnaḥ upasaṃpatprekṣaḥ paripūrṇaviṃśativarṣaḥ / eripūrṇamasya tricīvaraṃ pātraṃ / pariśuddhaṃ āntarāyikairdharmairātmānaṃ vadati / soyamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena saṃghādupasaṃpadaṃ yācate / sacetsaṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyātsaṃgho yatsaṃghaḥ evaṃnāmānaṃ upasaṃpādayet evaṃnāmnopādhyāyena / eṣā jñaptiḥ /
body.translated_text: May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. This so-and-so, of such-and-such [preceptor], is a candidate for <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination). This so-and-so requests from the <s>Saṅgha</s> full ordination with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor). If it is the proper time and the <s>Saṅgha</s> approves, let the <s>Saṅgha</s> consent that we question so-and-so in the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s> regarding the obstructive conditions (<s>āntarāyika dharmāḥ</s>), with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>. This is the <s>jñapti</s> (motion). Listen, venerable one: this is your [examination] — all as before. May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. This so-and-so, of such-and-such [preceptor], is a candidate for <s>upasaṃpad</s>; he has completed twenty years of age; his set of three robes (<s>tricīvara</s>) and bowl (<s>pātra</s>) are complete. He declares himself pure with regard to the obstructive conditions. This so-and-so, with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>, requests from the <s>Saṅgha</s> full ordination. If it is the proper time and the <s>Saṅgha</s> approves, let the <s>Saṅgha</s> consent to fully ordain so-and-so with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>. This is the <s>jñapti</s> (motion).

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ ayamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmnaḥ upasaṃpatprekṣaḥ puruṣaḥ paripūrṇaviṃśativarṣaḥ / paripūrṇamasya tricīvaraṃ pātraṃ ca / pariśuddhamāntarāyikairdharmaiḥ ātmānaṃ vadati / so 'hamevanāmnā upādhyāyena saṃghādupasaṃpadaṃ yācate tatsaṃghaḥ evaṃnāmānaṃ upasaṃpādayati evaṃnāmnā upādhyāyena / yeṣāmāyuṣmatāṃ kṣamate evaṃnāmānaṃ upasaṃpādayituṃ evaṃnāmnā upādhyāyena te tūṣṇī / yeṣāṃ na kṣamate te bhāṣantām / iyaṃ prathamā karmavācanā / evaṃ dvirapi trirapi / upasaṃpadyate saṃghena evaṃnāmā evanāmnopādhyayena kṣāntamanujñātaṃ yasmāttūṣṇīṃ evaṃ etaddhārayāmi / śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman catvāra ime tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatena arhatā samyak saṃbuddhena evaṃ pravrajitopasaṃpannasya bhikṣirniḥśrayā ākhyātā yaṃ niḥśritya bhikṣoḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / utsahase tvamevaṃnāmā yāvajjīvaṃ pāṃsukulena cīvareṇa yāpayitum / utsahe / atirekalābhaḥ paṭirvā prāvaro vā kośeyo vā āmilakā vā kṛmivarṇā vā samavarṇā vā durvarṇā vā ūrṇaṃ vā ūrṇakaṃ vā śāṇakaṃ vā kṣomakaṃ vā kārpāsikaṃ vā dukulaṃ vā kautmapakaṃ vā parāntakaṃ vā iti yadvā punaranyadapi kalpikaṃ cīvaraṃ saṃghādvā utpadyate pudgalato vā tatrāpi te pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā / kaścidevaṃrūpaṃ sthānamabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbhotsye / śṛṇu tvamevaṃnāman piṇḍapātaṃ ca bhojanānāṃ kalpikaṃ sulabhaṃ niḥśritya bhikṣoḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / utsahase tvamevaṃnāmā yāvajjīvaṃ piṇḍapātena bhojanena yāpayitum / utsahe / atirekalābhaḥ bhaktāni vā tarpaṇāni vā yavāgūḥ pānāni va pāñcamikaṃ vā āṣṭamikaṃ vā cāturdaśikaṃ vā pāñcadaśikaṃ vā naityikaṃ vā nimantraṇakaṃ vā otpātikaṃ vā iti utpiṇḍaṃ vā iti yadvā punaranyadapi kalpikaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ saṃghādvā utpadyate pudgalato vā tatrāpi te pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā / kaścidevaṃrūpaṃ sthānaṃ abhisaṃbhotsye / abhisaṃbhotsye /
body.translated_text: May the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear. This so-and-so, of such-and-such [preceptor], is a man who is a candidate for <s>upasaṃpad</s>; he has completed twenty years of age. His set of three robes (<s>tricīvara</s>) and bowl (<s>pātra</s>) are complete. He declares himself pure with regard to the obstructive conditions. He, with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>, requests from the <s>Saṅgha</s> full ordination. The <s>Saṅgha</s> fully ordains so-and-so with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>. Those venerable ones who approve of fully ordaining so-and-so with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s> should remain silent. Those who do not approve should speak. This is the first <s>karmavācanā</s> (formal proclamation). [Likewise a second and third time.] So-and-so has been fully ordained by the <s>Saṅgha</s> with such-and-such as <s>upādhyāya</s>; it is approved and consented to, since they are silent. Thus I record it. Listen, venerable one: these are the four <s>niśrayas</s> (resources) declared by the Blessed One, the Knower and Seer, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for one who has thus gone forth and been fully ordained as a <s>bhikṣu</s> — relying upon which a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s going forth, full ordination, and <s>bhikṣu</s>-status exist in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Can you, so-and-so, sustain yourself for life with rag-robes (<s>pāṃśukula cīvara</s>) as clothing? I can. The surplus gain is: a robe-cloth, or a cloak, or silk, or <s>āmilakā</s> cloth, or worm-colored, or uniform-colored, or coarse-colored, or woolen, or fine wool, or hemp, or flax, or cotton, or <s>dukūla</s> (muslin), or <s>kautmapaka</s>, or <s>parāntaka</s> — or whatever other allowable robe arises from the <s>Saṅgha</s> or from an individual; even in accepting that, moderation should be observed by you. Can you endure such a condition? I can endure it. Listen, so-and-so: relying on <s>piṇḍapāta</s> (alms-food), the allowable and easily obtained among foods, a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s going forth, full ordination, and <s>bhikṣu</s>-status exist in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Can you, so-and-so, sustain yourself for life with alms-food as sustenance? I can. The surplus gain is: cooked meals, or nourishing drinks, or rice-gruel, or beverages, or the fifth-day offering, or the eighth-day offering, or the fourteenth-day offering, or the fifteenth-day offering, or a regular offering, or an invitation, or an unexpected offering, or excess alms-food — or whatever other allowable alms-food arises from the <s>Saṅgha</s> or from an individual; even in accepting that, moderation should be observed by you. Can you endure such a condition? I can endure it.

body.text: śṛṇu tvamevaṃnāman vṛkṣamūlaṃ śayanāsanānāṃ kalpikaṃ vā sulabhaṃ ca yanniḥśritya bhikṣoḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / utsahase tvamevaṃnāman yāvajjīvaṃ vṛkṣamūlena śayanāsanena yāpayitum / utsahe / atirekalāmaḥ layanāni vā māṭā vā kūṭāgārāṇi vā harmyakā vā harmantikā vā āmalakapṛṣṭikā vā daṇḍañchadanāni vā phalakañchadanāni vā giriguhā vā prāgmāraguhā vā tṛṇakuṭikā vā parṇakuṭikā vā kṛtacaṃkramā vā akṛtacaṃkramā vā iti yadvā punaranyadapi kalpikaṃ śayanāsanaṃ saṃghādvā utpadyeta pudgalato vā tatrāpi te pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā / kaṃcidevaṃrūpaṃ sthānaṃ abhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbhotsye / śṛṇu tvamevaṃnāman pūtimutrabhaiṣajyānāṃ kalpikaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca yanniḥśritya bhikṣoḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ / utsahase tvamevaṃnāmā yāvajjīvaṃ pūtimutrena bhaiṣyajyena yāpayitum / utsahe / atirekalābhaḥ sarpistailaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ kālikaṃ yāmikaṃ sāptāhikaṃ yāvajjīvikaṃ mūlabhaiṣyajyaṃ gaṇḍabhaiṣajyaṃ patrabhaiṣajyaṃ puṣpabhaiṣajyaṃ phalabhaiṣyajyamiti yadvā punaranyadapi kalpikaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ saṃghādvā utpadyeta pudgalato vā tatrāpi te pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā / kaścidevaṃrūṣaṃ sthānamabhisaṃbhotsyase / abhisaṃbhotsye /
body.translated_text: Listen, so-and-so: the foot of a tree is the permissible and easily obtainable lodging (<s>śayanāsana</s>), depending on which a <s>bhikṣu</s> goes forth and receives full ordination in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Can you, so-and-so, sustain yourself for as long as you live with tree-root lodging? I can. As extra gain: dwelling houses, huts, pointed-roof buildings, upper chambers, mansions, small mansions, <s>āmalaka</s>-roofed buildings, thatched shelters, plank-roofed shelters, mountain caves, natural caves, grass huts, leaf huts, with or without walking paths—or whatever other permissible lodging may arise from the <s>Saṅgha</s> or from individuals, in accepting those too you should exercise moderation. Will you be able to endure such conditions? I will. Listen, so-and-so: putrid urine as medicine (<s>pūtimutrabheṣajya</s>) is the permissible and easily obtainable [requisite], depending on which a <s>bhikṣu</s> goes forth and receives full ordination in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Can you, so-and-so, sustain yourself for as long as you live with putrid urine as medicine? I can. As extra gain: ghee, oil, honey, molasses, that which is to be taken seasonally, during the day, for seven days, for life—root medicines, stem medicines, leaf medicines, flower medicines, fruit medicines—or whatever other permissible medicine may arise from the <s>Saṅgha</s> or from individuals, in accepting those too you should exercise moderation. Will you be able to endure such conditions? I will.

body.text: śṛṇu tvamevaṃnāmaṃścatāra ime tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyak saṃbuddhena evaṃ pravrajitopasaṃpannasya bhikṣoḥ patanīyā dharmā ākhyātāḥ yānadhyāpadyamāno bhikṣuḥ sahādhyāpattyā abhikṣurbhavatyaśramaṇaḥ aśākyaputrīyaḥ dhvasyate bhikṣubhāvāt hataśrāmaṇyam dhvastaṃ mathitaṃ patitaṃ parājitapratyudvāryamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyam / [tadyathā tālo mastakāchinnaḥ abhavyo haritatvāya abhavyo virūṭiṃ buiddhiṃ viphalatāmāpattum /] katame catvāraḥ / anekaparyāyeṇa kāmā vigarhitāḥ kāmātmayāḥ kāmaniyantikāḥ sādhyavaśakāmānāṃ prahāṇaṃ varṇitaṃ pratinisargāntībhāvaḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodhaḥ vyupaśamo āsamantataḥ stomito varṇitaḥ praśastaḥ / adyāgreṇa te āyuṣman saraktacittena mātṛgrāmaścakṣurupanidhāya na vyavalokayitavyaḥ / kaḥ punarvādī dvayadvayasamāpattyā abrahmacaryaṃ maithunaṃ dharmaṃ pratisevitum / uktaṃ caitadāyuṣman tena bhāgavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyak saṃbuddhena / yaḥ punarbhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ śikṣāsāmīcīṃ samāpannaḥ śikṣāmapratyākhyāya śikṣādaurvalyamanāviṣkṛtyābrahmacaryaṃ maithunaṃ dharmaṃ pratisevate antatastiryagyonigatayāpi sārdhaṃ evaṃrūpaṃ sthānamadhyāpadya sahādhyāpattyā abhikṣurbhavatyaśramaṇaḥ aśākyaputrīyaḥ dhvasyate bhikṣubhāvāt hataśrāmaṇyaṃ dhvastaṃ mathitaṃ patitaṃ parājitamapratyudvāryamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyam / tadyathā tālo mastakāchinnaḥ abhavyo viruḍhiṃ vṛddhiṃ vipulatāmapattum / atra te adyāgreṇa avadyācāreṇa adhyāpattyāvadyācāravairamaṇyā tīvracatesā ārakṣasmṛtyā pramāde yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / kaścidevaṃrūpasthānaṃ nādhyāpastyase / nādhyāpatsye /
body.translated_text: Listen, so-and-so: there are four <s>pārājika dharmas</s> (offenses entailing defeat) which have been declared by that <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), the Knower, the Seer, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has gone forth and been fully ordained in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who commits any of these, together with the offense, ceases to be a <s>bhikṣu</s>, is no <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), is no son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; he falls from the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>—his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (asceticism) is destroyed, ruined, crushed, fallen, defeated; his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> cannot be restored. [Just as a palm tree with its crown cut off is incapable of becoming green, incapable of sprouting, growing, and bearing fruit.] What are the four? In many ways sensual desires (<s>kāmas</s>) have been censured; those who pursue sensual desires, who are bound by sensual desires—the abandonment of sensual desires has been praised; cessation, fading away, end, calming—these have been fully extolled, praised, commended. From this day forward, venerable one, you should not look upon women with a lustful mind, how much less engage in the unchaste act of sexual intercourse. And it has been said, venerable one, by that <s>Bhagavat</s>, the Knower, the Seer, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: whoever, having taken the training and practice together with the <s>bhikṣus</s>, without renouncing the training and without declaring the weakness of the training, engages in the unchaste act of sexual intercourse, even with an animal—one who commits such an offense, together with the offense, ceases to be a <s>bhikṣu</s>, is no <s>śramaṇa</s>, is no son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; he falls from the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>—his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> is destroyed, ruined, crushed, fallen, defeated; his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> cannot be restored. Just as a palm tree with its crown cut off is incapable of sprouting, growing, and bearing abundant fruit. In this regard, from this day forward, you should make effort with intense endeavor, with careful mindfulness, in vigilance against shameful conduct and the offense of shameful conduct. Will you not commit such an offense? I will not.

body.text: śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman anekaparyāyeṇa bhagavatā adattādānaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ vigarhitaṃ adattādānavirati stutā stomitā varṇitā praśastā / adyāgreṇa te āyuṣman steyacittena tilatuṣamapi parakyamadattamādātavyaṃ kaḥ punarvādaḥ pañcamāṣikaṃ vā uttarapañcamāṣikaṃ vā / uktametadāyuṣmaṃstena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena / yaḥ punarbhikṣurgrāmagatamaraṇyagataṃ vā pareṣāṃ adattaṃ steyasaṃkhyātamādadīta yadrūpeṇādattādānena rājā vainaṃ gṛhītvā rājamātro vā hanyādvā saṃvadhrīyādvā pravāsayedvā evaṃ cainaṃ vadet- tvaṃ bhoḥ puiruṣa cauro 'si bālo 'si muḍho 'si steno 'sī tyevaṃrūpaṃ sthānamadhyāpadya sahādhyāpattyā abhikṣurbhavati [aśramaṇaḥ aśākyaputrīyaḥ dhvasyate bhikṣubhāvāt itaśrāmaṇyaṃ dhvastaṃ mathitaṃ patitaṃ parājitamapramyudvāryamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyaṃ /] tadyathā tālo mastakāchinnaḥ [abhavyo haritatvāya abhavyo viruḍhiṃ vṛddhiṃ vipulatāmāpattum / atra te adhyāgreṇa avadyācāreṇa adhyāpattyāvadyācāravairamaṇyāṃ tīvracetasā ārakṣāsmṛtyā pramāde yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / kiñcidevarūvaṃ sthānaṃ nādhyāpatsyase /] nādhyāpatsye / śṛṇu tvamevaṃnāman anekaparyayeṇa bhagavatā prāṇātipāto vigarhitaḥ prāṇātipātaviratiḥ stutā stomitā vanditā praśasta / adyāgreṇa te āyuṣman [saṃci]ntya kuntapipilako 'pi prāṇeṣu jīvitāt na vyaparopayitavyaḥ kaḥ punarvādo manuṣyavigrahaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: Listen, O long-lived one! In many ways the Blessed One has prohibited and condemned <s>adattādāna</s> (taking what is not given); abstention from taking what is not given has been praised, extolled, commended, and lauded. From today onward, O long-lived one, you must not take with thieving intent even so much as a sesame husk belonging to another that has not been given — how much more so something worth five <s>māṣas</s> or more than five <s>māṣas</s>! It has been declared, O long-lived one, by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: If any <s>bhikṣu</s> takes what is not given belonging to others, whether from a village or from the wilderness, with the intent of theft — of such a nature that for such taking of what is not given, a king having seized him, or a king's officer, would execute him, or imprison him, or banish him, and would say to him thus: 'You, fellow, are a thief! You are a fool! You are deluded! You are a robber!' — a <s>bhikṣu</s> who transgresses into such an offense, together with the transgression, ceases to be a <s>bhikṣu</s>, [is no longer a renunciant, is no longer a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; he falls from the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>; his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (asceticism) is destroyed, crushed, fallen, defeated, and irrecoverable.] Just as a palm tree with its crown cut off [is incapable of becoming green again, incapable of sprouting, growing, or becoming abundant. Henceforth you must, with intense mind and protective mindfulness, exert yourself against heedlessness in abstaining from blameworthy conduct and transgression. You shall not transgress into any such offense.] I shall not transgress. Listen, O so-and-so named one! In many ways the Blessed One has condemned <s>prāṇātipāta</s> (the taking of life); abstention from taking life has been praised, extolled, honored, and lauded. From today onward, O long-lived one, you must not intentionally deprive of life even an ant or a louse — how much more so a human being or one in human form!

body.text: uktaṃ caitadāyuṣmaṃstena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyak saṃbuddhena / yaḥ punarbhikṣumanuṣyaṃ vā manuṣmavigrahaṃ vā svahastena saṃcintya jīvitād vyaparopayet śasraṃ vaināmāghārayet śastradhārakaṃ vāsya paryeṣet maraṇāya vainaṃ samādāpayeta maraṇavarṇaṃ vāsyānusaṃvarṇayet / evaṃ cainaṃ vadet- haṃbhoḥ puruṣa kiṃ tvayā pāpakenāśucinā durjīvitena mṛtaṃ te bhoḥ puruṣa jīvitādvaramiticintānumataiścittasaṃkalpairanakeparyāyeṇa maraṇāya vainaṃ samādāpayet maraṇavarṇaṃ vāsya anusaṃvarṇayet sa ca tena kālaṃ kuryādityevaṃrūpo bhikṣuḥ sthānamadhyāpadya sahādhyāpattyā abhikṣurbhavati aśramaṇaḥ aśākyaputrīyaḥ [dhvasyate bhikṣumāvāt hataśrāmaṇyaṃ dhvastaṃ mathitaṃ patitaṃ parājitamapratyudvāryamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyam / tadyathā tālo mastakāchinnaḥ abhavyo haritvāya abhavyo viruḍhiṃ vṛddhiṃ vipulatāmapattum / adya te adyāgreṇa avadyācāreṇa adhyāpattyāvadyācāravairamaṇyāṃ tīvracetasā ārākṣasmṛtyā pramāde yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ kiñcidevarūpaṃ sthānaṃ nādhyāpatsyase / nādhyāpatsye /] śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman anekaparyāyeṇa bhagavatā mṛṣāvādo vigarhitaḥ mṛṣāvādaviratiḥ stutā stomitā vanditā praśastā /
body.translated_text: And it has been declared, O long-lived one, by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: If any <s>bhikṣu</s> intentionally deprives a human being or one in human form of life with his own hand, or provides a weapon for that person, or seeks a weapon-bearer for him, or urges him toward death, or praises the beauty of death to him — and says thus to him: 'Ho there, fellow! What use is this wretched, impure, wretched life to you? Death for you, O fellow, would be better than life!' — if by such thoughts, intentions, mental resolves, and various means he urges him toward death or praises the beauty of death to him, and that person thereby dies — a <s>bhikṣu</s> of such a nature, having transgressed into such an offense, together with the transgression, ceases to be a <s>bhikṣu</s>, is no longer a renunciant, is no longer a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; [he falls from the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>; his <s>śrāmaṇya</s> is destroyed, crushed, fallen, defeated, and irrecoverable. Just as a palm tree with its crown cut off is incapable of becoming green again, incapable of sprouting, growing, or becoming abundant. Henceforth you must, with intense mind and protective mindfulness, exert yourself against heedlessness in abstaining from blameworthy conduct and transgression. You shall not transgress into any such offense.] I shall not transgress. Listen, O long-lived one! In many ways the Blessed One has condemned <s>mṛṣāvāda</s> (false speech); abstention from false speech has been praised, extolled, honored, and lauded.

body.text: adyāgreṇa te āyuṣman hāsyaprekṣaṇo 'pi saṃprajānamṛṣāvāk na bhāṣitavyā kaḥ punarvādo 'santamasaṃvidyamānamuttarasanuṣyadharmaṃ pralapitum / uktaṃ caitat āyuṣman tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyak saṃbuddhena / yaḥ punarbhikṣu[ranabhijānannaparijānanna] santamasaṃvidyamānamuttaramanuṣyadharmamalamāryaviśeṣādhigamaṃ jñānaṃ vā darśanaṃ vā sparśavihāratāṃ vā pratijānīyādidaṃ jānāmīdaṃ paśyāmīti sa pareṇa samayena samanuyujyamāno vā asamanuyujyamāno vā āpanno viśurddhiṃ prekṣyaivaṃ vadedajānannevāhamāyuṣmanato 'vīcaṃ jānāmīti paśyāmiti[riktam tucchaṃ mṛṣāvyapalapanamanyatrābhimānāt ayamapi bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavatyasaṃvāsyaḥ /] ki jānāsi / duḥkhaṃ jānāmi / samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgaṃ jānāmi / kiṃ paśyasi / devān paśyāmi / nāgān yakṣān gandharvān kinnarān mahoragān pretān piśācān kumbhāṇḍān kaṭaputanān [paśyāmi / devāḥ api māṃ paśyanti / nāgāḥ yakṣāḥ gandharvāḥ kinnarāḥ mahoragāḥ pretāḥ piśācāḥ kunbhāṇḍāḥ kaṭapūtanāḥ api māṃ paśyanti / devānāṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇomi / nāgānāṃ yāvatkaṭapūtānāṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇomi / devāḥ api mama śabdam śṛṇvanti / nāgāḥ yāvatkaṭapūtanāḥ api mama śabdaṃ śṛṇvanti / devānāṃ darśanāya ḍapasaṃkramāmi / nāgānāṃ yāvatkaṭapūtānāṃ darśanāya upasaṃkramāmi / devāḥ api māṃ darśanāya upasaṃkrāmanti nāgāḥ yāvatkaṭapūtanāḥ api māṃ darśanāya upasaṃkrāmanti / devaiḥ sārdhamālapāmi saṃlapāmi pratisaṃmode sātatyaṃ samāpadye / nāgaiḥ yāvatkaṭapūtanaiḥ sārdhamālapāmi saṃlapāmi pratisaṃmode sātatyaṃ samāpadyae / devāḥ api mayā sārdhamālapanti saṃlapanti pratisaṃbhodante sātatyaṃ samāpadyante / nāgā yāvatkaṭapūtanāḥ api mayā sārdhamālapanti saṃlapanti pratisaṃmodante sātatyaṃ samāpadyante / alabhye vasan anityasaṃjñayā labhyohamasmi ityātmānaṃ pratijānīte / anitye duḥkhasaṃjñayā duḥkhe anātmasaṃjñayā āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñayā sarvaloke anabhiratisaṃjñayā ālokasaṃjñayā praharaṇasaṃjñayā virāgasaṃjñayā nirodhasaṃjñayā maraṇasaṃjñayā / alamye vasan aśubhasaṃjñayā na śubhasaṃjñayā alammohamasmi ityātmānaṃ pratijānīte / vinīlakasaṃjñayā vipūyakasaṃjñayā vyātmākakasaṃjñayā vipadmakasaṃjñayā vikhāditasaṃjñayā vilohitakasaṃjñayā vikṣiptakasaṃjñayā / asthisaṃjñayā śūnyatāpratyavīkṣaṇasaṃjñayā laśyo 'hamasmi iti pratijānīte /
body.translated_text: From this day forward, venerable one, even in jest you must not speak a deliberate falsehood — how much less so is it to be said of babbling about a superhuman <s>dharma</s> (attainment) that does not exist and is not present! For this has been spoken, venerable one, by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: 'Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, not truly knowing and not truly comprehending, claims a superhuman <s>dharma</s> — a noble and distinguished attainment — that does not exist and is not found in him, whether it be knowledge, or vision, or dwelling in meditative contact, saying "I know this, I see this" — that one, at a later time, whether questioned or not questioned, having fallen into the offense and seeking purification, speaks thus: "Not knowing, I said to the venerable ones that I know, that I see — that was empty, hollow, and a false claim — except through overestimation." That <s>bhikṣu</s> too is <s>pārājika</s> (defeated), not to be dwelt with.' What do you know? 'I know <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). I know <s>samudaya</s> (the origin), <s>nirodha</s> (the cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (the path).' What do you see? 'I see <s>devas</s> (gods). I see <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>kinnaras</s> (half-human beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating spirits), <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-shaped demons), and <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> (foul-smelling spirits). The <s>devas</s> too see me. The <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> too see me. I hear the voices of <s>devas</s>. I hear the voices of <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>. The <s>devas</s> too hear my voice. The <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> too hear my voice. I approach the <s>devas</s> to see them. I approach the <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> to see them. The <s>devas</s> too approach me to see me. The <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> too approach me to see me. I converse with the <s>devas</s>, I speak with them, I exchange greetings, and I attain continuous communion. I converse with the <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>, I speak with them, I exchange greetings, and I attain continuous communion. The <s>devas</s> too converse with me, speak with me, exchange greetings, and attain continuous communion. The <s>nāgas</s> through to the <s>kaṭapūtanas</s> too converse with me, speak with me, exchange greetings, and attain continuous communion.' Dwelling in the unattained, through the perception of impermanence, one claims 'I am one who has attained.' Through the perception of suffering in what is impermanent; through the perception of non-self in what is suffering; through the perception of repulsiveness in food; through the perception of non-delight in the whole world; through the perception of light; through the perception of abandonment; through the perception of dispassion; through the perception of cessation; through the perception of death — dwelling in the unattained, through the perception of the impure rather than the pure, one claims 'I am one freed from delusion': through the perception of the discolored corpse, through the perception of the festering corpse, through the perception of the dismembered corpse, through the perception of the bloated corpse, through the perception of the gnawed corpse, through the perception of the blood-smeared corpse, through the perception of the scattered corpse, through the perception of the skeleton, through the perception of contemplating emptiness — one claims 'I am one who has attained.'

body.text: alamye vasan prayamasya dhyānasya dvitīvasya tṛtīyasya caturthasya dhānayya maitryāḥ karuṇāyāḥ muditāyāḥ upekṣāyāḥ ākāśāntyāyatanasya vijñānānantyāyatanasya akiñcinyāyatanasya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasya srotāpattiphalasya sakṛdāgāmiphalasya anāgāmiphalasya [arhattvaphalasya] ṛddhiviṣayasya divassa śrotasya cetaḥparyāyasya pūrvanivāsasya cayutyupahānasya anarhanneva samāno 'hamasmi aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyī ityātmānaṃ pratijānīte / anyatra pratimānāt ityevaṃrūpaṃ bhikṣuḥ sthānamavapadya sahādhyāpattyā abhikṣurbhavati / aśramaṇaḥ aśākyaputrīyaḥ dhvasyate bhikṣubhāvāt hatamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyaṃ dhvastaṃ mathitaṃ patitaṃ parājitaṃ apratyudvāryamasya bhavati śrāmaṇyam / tadyathā tālo mastakācchinnaḥ abhavyo haritatvāya abhavyo virūḍhiṃ vṛddhiṃ vipulatāṃ āpattum / atra me adyāgreṇa anadhyācāre anadhyāpattyā anadhyācāravairamaṇyāṃ tīvracetasā ārakṣasmṛtyā pramāde yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / kiñcidevaṃ sthānamadhyāpatsye / nādhyāpatsye / [ime khalu patanīyā dharmā ākhyātāḥ / ataḥ śramaṇakārakāḥ dharmā ākhyātavyāḥ /] śṛṇu tvamāyuṣman catvāraḥ ime tena bhagavatā jānatā paśyatā tathāgatenārhatā samyak saṃbuddhena śramaṇakārakāḥ dharmāḥ ākhyātāḥ katame catvāraḥ / adyāgreṇa te āyuṣmatā-
body.translated_text: Enough of the dwelling in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the second, the third, the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>; of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity); of the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>); of the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), [the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhattvaphala</s>)]; of the domain of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), the knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>), the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>), the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapatti</s>) — [if] one who is not an <s>Arhat</s> declares of himself 'I am one who meditates on the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>),' except through overestimation — a <s>bhikṣu</s> who falls into such a condition, together with the offense, ceases to be a <s>bhikṣu</s>. He is not an ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>), not a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; he is expelled from the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>. His asceticism is destroyed, ruined, crushed, fallen, defeated; his asceticism is irrecoverable — just as a palm tree cut off at the top is incapable of becoming green again, incapable of reaching growth, increase, and abundance. From this day forward, may I be diligent in the avoidance of misconduct, in freedom from offense, in abstaining from misconduct, with an earnest mind, with watchful mindfulness, with regard to heedlessness. Will you fall into any such condition? I will not fall. [These are the offenses entailing defeat (<s>pārājika</s>) that have been declared. Now the qualities that make an ascetic (<s>śramaṇakāraka dharma</s>) should be declared.] Listen, venerable one: these are the four qualities that make an ascetic, declared by the Blessed One, the Knower and Seer, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. What are the four? From this day forward, venerable one —

children.text: ākruṣṭena na pratyākroṣṭavyam roṣitena na pratiroṣitavyam /
children.translated_text: When reviled, you should not revile in return; when angered, you should not show anger in return.

children.text: tāḍitena na pratitāḍitavyam bhaṇḍitena na pratibhaṇḍitavyam //
children.translated_text: When struck, you should not strike in return; when quarreled with, you should not quarrel in return.

body.text: kiñcidevaṃrūpaṃ sthānaṃ adhyāpatsyase / na adhyāpatsye / śṛṇu tvamāyutman yaste abhūt pūīrvamāśākaḥ kaścidahaṃ labheyaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ ca / satvametarhi pravrajitaṃ upasaṃpamnam pratirūpeṇa upādhyāyeṇa pratirūpābhyāmācāryābhyāṃ samagreṇa saṃghena [jña]pticaturthena karmaṇā akopyena anāsthāpanarheṇa yatra varṣaśatopasaṃpannena bhikṣuṇā śikṣāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ tatra tadahopasaṃpannena iti yatra samānaśīlatā samānaśikṣatā samānaprātimokṣasūtroddeśatā sā adyāgreṇa ārāgayitavyā na virāgayitavyā / adyāgreṇa te upādhyāsyāntike pitṛsaṃjñā sthāpayitavyā upādhyāyenāpi tavānnike putrasaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā adyāgreṇa te upādhyāyo yāvajjīvaṃ upasthāpayitavyaḥ / upādhyāyenāpi tvaṃ glānaḥ upasthāpayitavyaḥ āmaraṇāya vā vyutthānāya vā / adyāgreṇa te sagauraveṇa vihartavyam sapratiśeṇa sabhayavaśavarttinā sabrahmacāriṣu sthavireṣu madhyeṣu navakeṣu / adyāgreṇa te uddeṣṭavyam paṭhitavyaṃ svādhyāyitavyaṃ skandhakauśalyaṃ dhātukauśalyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ āyatanakauśalyaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ dhūḥca tena nikṣeptavyā aprāptasya prāptaye anadhigatasyādhigamāya asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai imāni ca te mayā audārikaudārikāni śikṣāpadāni ākhyātāni anyāni vā tāni anvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśe uddiśyamāne śroṣyasi anyāni ca te ācāryopādhyāyābhyāṃ grāhayiṣyanni / samānopādhyāyāḥ samānācāryāḥ āptakāḥ saṃlaptakāḥ saṃsutakā sapremakāḥ / eṣa tvamupasaṃpanno varaprajñasya śāsane / yathemāṃ na virāgayasi durlabhaṃ kṣaṇa[saṃpadam /] prāsādikaḥ pravrajyāpariśuddhasyopasaṃpadaḥ / ākhyātāḥ satyanāmnā vai saṃbuddhena prajānatā / eṣa tva[mupasaṃpanno] pramāde saṃpādaya //
body.translated_text: Will you fall into any such condition? I will not fall. Listen, venerable one: you formerly had a wish — 'May I obtain, in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, <s>pravrajyā</s> (going forth), <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination), and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>.' You have now gone forth and been fully ordained, in proper form, with a proper <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor), with proper <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers), by the complete <s>Saṅgha</s>, through a <s>jñapticaturtha karman</s> (act with motion as the fourth), irrevocable and not subject to reversal. Where a <s>bhikṣu</s> ordained for a hundred rainy seasons must train in the training, there one ordained on this very day must also train. Where there is equality of conduct, equality of training, and equality of the recitation of the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> — that, from this day forward, is to be cherished, not neglected. From this day forward, you must establish the perception of a father toward your <s>upādhyāya</s>, and the <s>upādhyāya</s> must establish the perception of a son toward you. From this day forward, your <s>upādhyāya</s> must be attended upon by you for as long as he lives. And the <s>upādhyāya</s> must attend upon you when you are ill, until death or recovery. From this day forward, you must dwell with respect, with deference, with fearful obedience, toward your fellow practitioners in the holy life — elders, middle-ranking, and junior. From this day forward, you must study, recite, and review: skill in the aggregates (<s>skandhakauśalya</s>), skill in the elements (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>), skill in the sense-bases (<s>āyatanakauśalya</s>), skill in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), skill in what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānakauśalya</s>). And you must bear the yoke for the attainment of what has not been attained, the realization of what has not been realized, the direct experience of what has not been directly experienced. These major training rules have been declared to you by me; others you will hear when the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> is recited every half-month; and still others your <s>ācārya</s> and <s>upādhyāya</s> will teach you. Those with the same <s>upādhyāya</s>, the same <s>ācārya</s> — they are trustworthy, they have been spoken with, they have been agreed upon, they are dear. You are now ordained in the teaching of the most excellent wisdom. May you not neglect this rare opportunity of favorable circumstances. The going forth is pleasing, the ordination is purified. Declared indeed by the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One), bearing the name of truth, the all-knowing one. You are now ordained — strive with regard to heedlessness!
